_about: Curated findings shown at the top of each device's dashboard page (analysis/dashboard_summary.py), below the auto-generated statements. status: 'verified' = backed by the evidence given; 'hypothesis' = plausible, not yet confirmed (say how to confirm). device is a glob on device_id. Numbers here are hand-written: re-check them whenever the device's data is re-collected (date says when they were last checked).

notes.title: Llama decode measures the memory system only after two fixes
notes.text: Generating one token at a time should be limited by reading the weights. Two harness problems hid that: (1) PyTorch's fused attention kernel tiles over query tokens, so with one query most of each tile was idle (47% of the step at batch 1, 64% at batch 8), and (2) each step issues ~500 small kernels from Python, which this node's 2016 Xeon could not launch as fast as the GPU ran them. Decode attention is now two batched matmuls over an in-place KV cache, and decode is also timed replayed from a CUDA graph (as serving engines run it). llama3.2-1b fp32: batch 1 66.8 → 117.6 tokens/s, batch 8 251 → 678.5 tokens/s.

notes.title: Clock speed explains the GEMM gap to the datasheet
notes.text: GEMM reached 14.1 TFLOP/s fp32 against a 15.7 datasheet figure. The datasheet assumes the 1530 MHz boost clock; under its 300 W power limit this GPU ran GEMM at ~1392 MHz (15.34 × 1392/1520 = 14.05 matches the September legacy run, which held 1520 MHz). Clocks are recorded, not locked. Because the ceiling is measured at whatever clock that GEMM ran at, a kernel that ran faster can exceed it slightly: Llama prefill ran at ~1493 MHz and shows 103% of the measured GEMM peak.

notes.title: Small problems can beat the memory ceiling
notes.text: Sizes whose data fits in the 6 MB L2 cache are not limited by HBM bandwidth (SAXPY n=1M: 1,010 GB/s vs the 845 GB/s ceiling). The ceiling markers are drawn only for problems that stream from device memory.

notes.title: Irregular sparse workloads sit far below the bandwidth line
notes.text: SpMV on a regular 3-D Poisson matrix reaches 78% of bandwidth, but on a power-law matrix only 9%, and SpGEMM 2–9%: random gathers and the symbolic phase (inside the timer, by design) waste most of each memory transaction. These are cuSPARSE results as measured; the 'bandwidth-bound' label does not hold for them.

notes.title: What the 16 GB Volta card cannot run
notes.text: Volta has no bf16 hardware, so every bf16 row is recorded 'unsupported' instead of emulated. Problems are skipped before running when 2.5× their working set exceeds ~14 GB of usable memory: Llama-3.2-3B and Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.2-1B decode at batch 32, SAXPY n=1G, LBM n=512 and AES on 4 GB. The 2.5× safety margin is conservative; some of the 8–9 GB problems would probably fit (open item).

notes.title: SHA-256 may be below well-tuned GPU code
notes.text: The custom CUDA SHA-256 reaches 52–105 GB/s. Each thread reads its own message, so loads are not coalesced; a layout that interleaves messages may be much faster. To confirm: profile with Nsight Compute (memory throughput vs instruction throughput) before using C9 in a CPU-GPU ratio.
